changes.summary: Interior completed the first American Samoa offshore-minerals auction, producing $6 million in provisional high bids while preserving post-sale issuance, environmental-review and activity-approval limits.
A federal judge preliminarily limited the USDA secretary's official religious communications while preserving voluntary faith discussion and leaving appeal and final merits unresolved.
After trial, a federal judge vacated Ryan White funding conditions and permanently enjoined their use against plaintiff organizational members.
DOJ asked the Ninth Circuit to treat its Alaska election-certification appeal as moot, vacate the standing dismissal and remand; the court had not ruled by cutoff.

evidence_extracts.american_samoa: The official sale release reports $6 million in high bids and expressly states that lease issuance would not authorize delineation, testing or mining.
evidence_extracts.usda_religious_messages: The preliminary injunction adopts boundaries from USDA's own policy while preserving appropriate voluntary religious discussion and invitations.
evidence_extracts.ryan_white: The post-trial order vacates the challenged conditions and permanently enjoins the government from imposing them or similar conditions on plaintiff organizational members.
evidence_extracts.alaska_appeal: DOJ's brief asks for Munsingwear vacatur and remand on mootness grounds; it is not an appellate disposition.
